original_question: (F. Lisi, L. Sabatini). Let G be a non-trivial finite group and let p1,..., pk be the distinct prime divisors of |G|. For each i, let Hi be a Sylow pi-subgroup of G. Is it true that there exists an element x ∈ G such that for all i the subgroup Hi ∩ Hix is inclusion-minimal in {Hi ∩ Hig: g ∈ G}?
target_in_paper: Problem 21.26 in the section "New Problems (21st issue, 2026)"; the draft is essentially the paper's exact wording. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1401.0300.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft already matches the official problem almost verbatim: it has the correct ambient category (non-trivial finite groups), the correct primes (the distinct prime divisors of |G|), fixed Sylow p_i-subgroups H_i, a single element x required to work simultaneously for every i, and minimality with respect to inclusion among the intersections H_i ∩ H_i^g. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1401.0300.pdf))
missing_details: For a fully stand-alone formulation, define the conjugation notation explicitly, e.g. H_i^x := x^{-1}H_i x; the paper states the problem using H_i^x without a local notation clause. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1401.0300.pdf))

It helps to unpack "inclusion-minimal" as "minimal with respect to subgroup inclusion among {H_i ∩ g^{-1}H_i g : g ∈ G}", so it is clear that the question is not about minimum order and does not require uniqueness of the minimal intersection. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1401.0300.pdf))
refined_question: Let G be a non-trivial finite group, let p_1,\dots,p_k be the distinct prime divisors of |G|, and for each i fix a Sylow p_i-subgroup H_i of G. Is it true that there exists a single element x \in G such that, for every i=1,\dots,k, the subgroup H_i \cap x^{-1}H_i x is minimal with respect to inclusion among the family {H_i \cap g^{-1}H_i g : g \in G}?
justification: arXiv:1401.0300 is the Kourovka Notebook rather than a conventional single-topic article with an introduction and numbered theorems. The draft clearly targets Problem 21.26, and there is no nearby theorem, proposition, or alternate formulation attached to it; accordingly, the most paper-faithful refinement is to keep the statement essentially unchanged while only making the conjugation notation and the meaning of inclusion-minimal explicit. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300))
